title: Rapid POC: Network Partition Resilience Lab
summary: Hands-on lab to validate Redwood inference behavior under simulated network partitions and partial region outages. Focuses on failover policies, KV cache correctness, throughput degradation patterns, and observable signals for SLOs. Intended as a rapid POC for customers considering Dedicated or Private deployments with strict availability needs.
audience: Solutions engineers, platform reliability engineers, customer SREs, and technical PMs who will run a short on-site or remote workshop with a customer to demonstrate resilience properties and create reproducible test artifacts.
estimated_duration: 3 hours (can be split into two 90-minute sessions). Includes setup, guided scenarios, and a wrap-up analysis.
prerequisites: Kubernetes cluster with 3 worker nodes (can be minikube/k3s for lab), kubectl configured, Docker, access to a Redwood Dedicated test pool or emulated local runtime, Prometheus + Grafana installed or access to metrics endpoints, a load generator (vegeta or vegeta-setup script), basic familiarity with iptables/tc for network shaping.
objectives: 1) Demonstrate graceful model variant fallback when one region/node loses connectivity. 2) Observe KV cache warming behavior and correctness after partition healing. 3) Verify routing policies (latency-first vs cost-first) under partial outages. 4) Produce actionable telemetry and a short incident playbook customers can reuse.
workshop-outline: Intro (10m): goals and safety/rollback checklist. Setup (30m): clone repo, deploy local harness, register test model, verify baseline latencies. Scenario 1 - Single-node partition (30m): isolate worker A, validate fallback to worker B and cold-start impact. Scenario 2 - Region-level partial outage (30m): simulate high-latency links between zones and test policy-driven routing. Scenario 3 - KV cache corruption/invalidation (30m): kill cache process and ensure correctness after rebuild. Metrics & debugging (20m): inspect traces, token-level latencies, failed request patterns. Wrap-up (10m): findings, customer action items, next steps.
safety_and_rollback: Always start experiments on non-production test pools. Keep automated rollback scripts (kubectl rollout undo, redeploy envoy) in the harness. If network shaping persists, run reset-network.sh from the repo root. Keep contact info for platform infra on-call.
lab-exercises: Exercise A - Baseline measurement: run vegeta at 20 qps for 10 minutes, record p50/p95/p99 and token cost per request. Exercise B - Node partition: on node-1 run 'tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 250ms loss 2%' and observe routing. Exercise C - Failover policy test: switch routing policy from latency-first to cost-first and replay load. Exercise D - Cache warm/cold: flush KV cache (redis-cli FLUSHALL or stop the cache pod) then replay requests and measure tail latency and token overhead. Exercise E - Canary rollback: perform a canary deployment introducing a latency-increasing change and exercise automatic fallback to the stable variant.
observability_checks: Dashboards: model route latency, token-level breakdown, KV hit ratio, request error rate. Traces: follow a single request ID across fronting proxy -> router -> model-serving pod. Logs: look for 'fallback triggered' events, cache-miss spikes, and heartbeat timeouts. Alerts to set during POC: sustained p95 > 3x baseline, cache miss rate > 30%, fallback rate > 5%.
sample-code-snippets:
# sample: add network delay on linux node
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 250ms loss 2%

# reset network shaping
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root || true

# vegeta attack script example
echo 'POST http://redwood-local:8080/generate' > targets.txt
cat <<EOF >> targets.txt
@-
EOF
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=20 -duration=10m | vegeta report

# sample kube command to scale model-serving pool
kubectl scale deployment/model-serving-pool --replicas=3 -n redwood-test

# simple harness snippet to toggle routing policy (bash)
curl -X POST http://redwood-local:8080/admin/routing 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"policy":"cost_first"}'

# verify kv cache hits via redis-cli
redis-cli -h redis-svc info | grep keyspace
reference-implementation-notes: Implementation in the accompanying GitHub repo uses a small adapter service (go) that simulates tokenized responses with configurable processing time. The harness integrates Envoy for fronting and a tiny router that mimics Redwood policy evaluation (headers-based). For Dedicated/Private customers we replace the adapter with the actual model-serving endpoint and run the same network-shaping steps in a staging VPC to reproduce region-level latencies.
common-findings-and-actions: Finding: sudden p99 spikes on failover due to cold KV cache leading to doubled token costs. Action: enable prefix caching for common prompts and pre-warm during canaries. Finding: routing policy change to cost-first increased tail latency in 10% of traces. Action: add latency guardrails and a rolling-window SLO check to prevent harmful policy flips. Finding: opaque errors from third-party proxies during partitions. Action: add explicit retry with idempotency keys and instrumented fallbacks.
deliverables-to-customer: 1) A runbook PDF (auto-generated from this doc) with commands and rollback steps. 2) Repro script in GitHub repo that runs all scenarios and dumps raw metrics. 3) Short slide deck summarizing results and recommended configuration changes. 4) JSON export of Grafana dashboards used for the workshop.
next-steps-and-checklist: - Confirm customer test pool credentials and non-prod cluster. - Schedule 2-hour workshop slot. - Share repo and pre-work checklist. - Run the harness at least once internal to validate scripts. - Fill the incident playbook with customer contacts and escalation path.
notes_to_self: Keep an eye on kernel-based network shaping differences across cloud providers (GCP vs AWS vs on-prem). Some managed networking layers will ignore tc rules; for those use a sidecar network proxy or run shaping inside a small VM acting as a traffic mirror. Capture a trace sample for every scenario and attach to JIRA ticket. Consider adding an automated KV pre-warm step in the next iteration.
conclusion: This lab produces reproducible evidence about how Redwood routing and cache strategies behave under network partitions and region degradation. The artifacts and runbook are intended to accelerate customer confidence during procurement of Dedicated or Private deployments and to feed back into default policy recommendations for high-availability workloads.
